name: splash
title: First-paint splash screen
summary: A branded loading screen that paints before JavaScript, never flashes on a cached visit, and can never block clicks.
when: The landing page is heavy (video, big bundle) and a cold first visit shows a blank screen for a noticeable moment.

lines: /* splash pack: paints before any JavaScript, removed by src/main.tsx
after React's first paint. Starts invisible and fades in after 240ms,
so a cached repeat visit (React mounted well before that) never sees
it at all: the delay IS the cache test. Token fallbacks cover dev,
where the stylesheet arrives with the JS. */
/* aria-hidden and covering everything: it must never catch a press,
or a splash that failed to leave makes the page unclickable. */
/* splash pack: take the loading screen down once React has painted.
Two frames: the first runs after React's commit, the second after the
browser PAINTED it (removing on the first can flash white on a slow
device). rAF never runs in a background tab, so a timer clears a hidden
tab's splash; a visible tab has painted by then and finds nothing left. */

next: Change the splash text in index.html (#splash p) to your site's name or wordmark.
